pr_title: drivers: stm32: use IF_ENABLED() macro in config structs
pr_body:
Use the IF_ENABLED() macro to increase readability in some of the STM32 drivers.

Fixes #62962
pr_comments:
Change looks good to me.
Before officially approving, I'll just run a couple of tests (compilation mostly) to be sure we didn't break anything.

> Fixes #62962

Are there any other STM32 drivers where this applies? If yes, then "Fixes"  should be changed to "Relates" or similar to avoid automatic issue closure.

issue_context.title: STM32: Investigate use of IF_ENABLED() to increase drivers readability
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
IF_ENABLED() was introduced after most of the STM32 drivers were implemented.
I propose to revisit drivers implementation and use IF_ENABLED when it increases readability.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Keep current code.

**Additional context**
Example use in STM32 SPI driver:

```
#if DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32_spi_subghz)
#define STM32_SPI_USE_SUBGHZSPI_NSS_CONFIG(id)				\
	.use_subghzspi_nss = DT_INST_PROP_OR(				\
			id, use_subghzspi_nss, false),
#else
#define STM32_SPI_USE_SUBGHZSPI_NSS_CONFIG(id)
#endif

#define STM32_SPI_INIT(id)						\
[...]
									\
static const struct spi_stm32_config spi_stm32_cfg_##id = {		\
	.spi = (SPI_TypeDef *) DT_INST_REG_ADDR(id),			\
	.pclken = pclken_##id,						\
	.pclk_len = DT_INST_NUM_CLOCKS(id),				\
	.pcfg = PINCTRL_DT_INST_DEV_CONFIG_GET(id),			\
	STM32_SPI_IRQ_HANDLER_FUNC(id)					\
	STM32_SPI_USE_SUBGHZSPI_NSS_CONFIG(id)				\
};
```

Could be replaced by : 
```

#define STM32_SPI_INIT(id)						\
[...]
									\
static const struct spi_stm32_config spi_stm32_cfg_##id = {		\
	.spi = (SPI_TypeDef *) DT_INST_REG_ADDR(id),			\
	.pclken = pclken_##id,						\
	.pclk_len = DT_INST_NUM_CLOCKS(id),				\
	.pcfg = PINCTRL_DT_INST_DEV_CONFIG_GET(id),			\
	STM32_SPI_IRQ_HANDLER_FUNC(id)					\
	IF_ENABLED(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32_spi_subghz), \
	(.use_subghzspi_nss = DT_INST_PROP_OR(id, use_subghzspi_nss, false),)) \
};
```

review_comments:
I would normally write this as

```c
IF_ENABLED(CONFIG_I2C_STM32_BUS_RECOVERY, (                     \
.scl = GPIO_DT_SPEC_INST_GET_OR(index, scl_gpios, {0}),         \
.sda = GPIO_DT_SPEC_INST_GET_OR(index, sda_gpios, {0}),         \
))                                                              \
IF_ENABLED(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32_i2c_v2), (        \
.timings = (const struct i2c_config_timing *)i2c_timings_##index, \
.n_timings = ARRAY_SIZE(i2c_timings_##index),                   \
))                                                              \
```

there's no hard guideline but that what looks more readable to me since the IF_ENABLED behaves like a `#ifdef` and we don't indent on that, and that would leave the field indented as they should rather than making it look they are nested in a lower level. How would you feel about that? @erwango 

blocking since you have a stray tab after `scl =`

Actually, this was the initial indentation, which I requested to update to the current version.

Rationale was about readability, which isn't great in those sections since they are generally not covered by syntactic highlighting. To me adding indentation allows to better distinguish between conditions and actual structure assignments.
...though it'd be great if you could fix that stray tab @ggrs, sorry I can't unsee it now :-)

same suggestion as above

```c
IF_ENABLED(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32_spi_subghz), (    \
.use_subghzspi_nss = DT_INST_PROP_OR(id, use_subghzspi_nss, false), \
))                                                              \
```
